findings.evidence: The accessory card now shows its title, prescription and the two 40x10 chips. The fixed footer ('saved 6/6 sets', Skip day, Note, Finish workout) still clips the bottom of that card. The Rest/Start/Reset row is hidden. Warm-up and Main lift each keep a header strip plus a full card, so all three exercises still do not fit at 390x844.
findings.userConsequence: The user must scroll to reach the third exercise's rest timer and note. The overall session state is clear, but a one-screen view of the day is not achieved. This is better than round 3, where the set chips were hidden too.
findings.suggestedChange: Fold the section label into the card's top border or the exercise title row. Alternatively, let the footer collapse to a single Finish button with a Note/Skip overflow, so the third card's rest row clears the fold.

findings.evidence: The accessory prescription reads 'rest 90s' on desktop, and the Main lift reads 'rest 2:00'. Its rest control shows '1:30'. The warm-up shows 'Set rest' with no duration. The response defends this as equivalent notation.
findings.userConsequence: Two formats for one value in the same card cost a moment of reconciliation. This is a recurring wording inconsistency, not an error.
findings.suggestedChange: Render the control and the prescription chip in one duration format, for example '1:30' in both places. Keep free text and ranges verbatim.

findings.evidence: The header says '1 total · 0 active · 1 draft'. The filter chips offer all/draft/completed/archived but no 'active' chip. The row says 'Plan: Draft' in small grey 12–13px text, and the routine overview shows the same 'Plan: Draft' as plain text. There is no section label for the active routine here, because there is no active routine.
findings.userConsequence: '0 active' is counted but cannot be filtered. The draft status that explains why Today has no active program is easy to read past. DeepSeek raised this in round 3 and it is only partly resolved.
findings.suggestedChange: Either add the 'active' chip or drop the active count from the header when it is zero. Give 'Plan: Draft' a visible badge or a one-line 'Activate to start' hint on the overview.

findings.evidence: Week 2 now opens as the selected week and the 'Next: Lower body · Week 2' button agrees with it. Mon carries a blue 'Next workout' text label. Every day row still has an identical outlined 'View day' button, so the next workout's button has no extra weight. The tab sublabels 'Selected' and 'View week' say nothing about progress, such as done or next.
findings.userConsequence: The right week is shown, but the next-workout label is a small text cue. A user scanning the buttons sees three equal actions.
findings.suggestedChange: Mark the next day's row with a filled or tinted 'Start' button. Replace the 'View week' sublabels with progress such as '3/3 done' and 'Next'.

findings.evidence: Resolve has larger controls (Keep as custom, checkbox, Choose version, search). The imported-strength caption and 'used 4 times' are small, and more than a third of the screen is blank below. The disabled 'Review import →' is faint grey. On Confirm, the sticky Save bar cuts through the third workout card. 'Edit workout →' is tiny inline text inside each day card. The 'Review' button on the review note is easy to confuse with the 'Review import' step.
findings.userConsequence: The path works and the validation message is clear. The small captions and the clipped day card read as unfinished compared with the rest of the flow.
findings.suggestedChange: Raise the captions to 13px. Add bottom padding or a scroll cue so the sticky bar does not clip a card. Make 'Edit workout' a padded text button and name the note action 'Resolve names'.

findings.evidence: Edit now has a visible label on the Body card. The avatar header still has only a faint pencil icon. The bodyweight line has point markers and a 168–169 lb range, but it is almost flat with no y-axis values. The Body card's age/height/weight labels are small and faint. Weight sits alone under age, leaving an empty cell.
findings.userConsequence: Editing is discoverable on the cards. Bodyweight reads mostly through the text line, and the chart adds little. The faint labels are the least legible tier on the page.
findings.suggestedChange: Label the header Edit as well. Add min and max tick labels to the chart. Use a darker label colour and a consistent grid in the Body card.

findings.evidence: Library rows are clear and the 'needs review' row now says 'Confirm names to link exercise history.' Category names are lowercase, previews are truncated, and the filter chips wrap to two rows and use up the first fold. Workspace now shows Theme above the Local-first card, but its theme chips wrap, with 'midnight' alone on a second row. The solid-black 'Download backup file' row and the red-outlined 'Import workspace' row outweigh Snapshot and Theme.
findings.userConsequence: Both screens work. Library takes extra scrolling before the list. Workspace puts destructive and backup actions at the same visual weight as ordinary settings.
findings.suggestedChange: Use a single scrolling row of chips or a select. Capitalise the category labels. Make Import workspace a quieter outlined row and confirm it only on tap.

findings.evidence: Desktop Routines is one row in an otherwise empty page, with Open grouped beside the name and the rest of the pane blank. The builder and routine map leave more than a third of the phone screen empty. The map's tiles are dense 'N sections / N exercises' text with no completion state. The desktop content column is about 840px, with the sidebar at 16–208px.
findings.userConsequence: The empty areas reflect sparse data, not a defect. The map does not show which weeks or days are done, so it is less useful than the overview.
findings.suggestedChange: Show done/next state on the map tiles. A sparse-state hint on desktop Routines, such as 'Import a routine from Prompts', would help.

strengths: Today onboarding is a clear 3-step path with one dark primary action and a manual-build escape hatch.
Workout set values are large mono chips, and the warm-up bodyweight chip now matches the others.
Header, prescription and tools are well grouped inside each exercise card. The sticky footer states 'saved 6/6 sets' and Finish workout is the dominant action.
History rows now have chevrons and separators, which gives a clear action cue. Sort and filter chips are clear.
Export for AI has a one-column mobile layout, a readable preview and Copy/Download actions.
Import error recovery offers a 'Copy recovery prompt' action. The offline copy/paste AI workflow stays prominent (Prompts, Import).
Light and terminal themes keep hierarchy, selection state and semantic accents (green next, amber warning, red destructive) at parity.
The desktop shell is stable, with the sidebar position unchanged across pages. Desktop workout fits the whole day without scrolling.
limitations: Review is of the frozen 27 static captures at 390x844 and 1280x900 only. No keyboard, screen-reader, persistence or responsive behavior outside those viewports was checked.
Contrast was judged by eye only. No ratios were measured. Small grey text at 11–13px is a visual concern, not a measured failure.
Lower folds of scrolled pages (Today bottom, Prompts, Profile, Library, Workspace) are not visible in the captures.
Source was not inspected. The comparison to earlier rounds relies on their JSON findings and assessments. Baseline screenshots were not reopened.

findings.evidence: Workout prescriptions, History/More, Add set and timer actions retain a similarly subdued green-gray treatment. Library previews and counts use the same muted tier. All are readable, but task instructions and actions are less immediately distinct than exercise names and entered values. This prior objection remains.
findings.userConsequence: Reading the prescription and finding secondary logging actions requires closer attention during a workout.
findings.suggestedChange: Strengthen task-relevant secondary text slightly, especially prescriptions and timer actions, while keeping optional catalog previews subordinate.

findings.evidence: The Body card now has a visible Edit label, but the Alex Morgan identity row still ends with a small, faint pencil alone.
findings.userConsequence: Editing the profile name is less discoverable than editing the other profile fields, and the control treatment is inconsistent within the page.
findings.suggestedChange: Use the same pencil-plus-Edit treatment beside the identity row.

findings.evidence: The equal-width export fields are clear, but the raw preview wraps session headings and set records across several lines. The metadata preamble occupies much of the visible preview before the first workout, whose heading breaks between the day name and completion status.
findings.userConsequence: Copying is straightforward, but checking the actual workout content remains slower than checking the export scope and counts.
findings.suggestedChange: Provide a compact readable session preview above expandable raw text, preserving the complete copied and downloaded content.

strengths: Onboarding clearly distinguishes the current step, later actions and the manual builder alternative.
Prompts makes Copy prompt prominent and explains the external AI chat and return-to-Import workflow.
Import recovery, exercise resolution and confirmation communicate distinct next actions. Confirmation explains the saved Squat link and optional further review.
All three exercises' entered set values are visible above the mobile workout footer. The earlier accessory-set visibility objection is resolved without sacrificing readable values.
Routine overview selects Week 2 and marks Lower body as Next workout. Plan: Draft is consistent between list and overview.
History rows now have separators and chevrons. Sorting labels and export filters are clear.
Desktop navigation and content placement are consistent across all four captures. Routine Open is grouped within a shorter span.
Workspace exposes theme choices with the correct visible selection in both themes, prioritizes backup and distinguishes destructive import.
Profile supplies weight dates, actual values and point markers. The builder explains unfinished routines, and the session summary has a clear next action.
The prior requests to invent a warm-up rest duration or remove Skip day are not supported by a visible usability failure in these captures.
limitations: Opened all 27 manifest files directly with the image-viewing tool. Every image was readable.
Read findings from all twelve prior reviews, all four prior assessments and the round 04 implementation response. No other current-round output or parent conversation was consulted.
Earlier screenshots were not reopened. Comparisons concern documented prior objections; no direct image-to-image regression claim is made. No new major issue was established.
Contrast judgments are visual only. No contrast ratios or accessibility conformance were measured.
Static screenshots cannot establish keyboard behavior, accessible names, touch target bounds, persistence, data safety or scrolling behavior.
Evidence covers 390x844 mobile and 1280x900 desktop, with four dark screens. Content outside the captured viewports was not inspected.
No source inspection, live app interaction, app mutation, file edits, installation, commits, pushes or delegation was performed.

findings.evidence: The Routines summary reads '1 total · 0 active · 1 draft', and the filter row offers all/draft/completed/archived with no Active filter or section, while the row says 'Plan: Draft' and the overview shows 'Next: Lower body · Week 2' after three logged weeks. 'New routine' is the only filled button; the existing plan's Open is an outlined control inside the row.
findings.userConsequence: A user who is already training this plan cannot tell what makes a routine 'active' or isolate one, and the page's strongest emphasis points at creating another routine rather than continuing.
findings.suggestedChange: Explain the plan state as 'Draft plan' with one line on what active means, add an Active filter or remove the active count until that state is reachable, and give the current plan's Open action weight closer to New routine.

findings.evidence: Prescription lines, History/More controls, and Library previews and counts use a subdued green-grey that is dimmer than the baseline dark capture opened for comparison. Text remains legible, but this tier sits closest to decoration and is weaker than the equivalent light-theme text.
findings.userConsequence: Prescriptions and catalog previews need closer reading at phone size, and the separation between task text and tertiary metadata is less clear than in the light theme.
findings.suggestedChange: Raise the secondary foreground one step in the terminal theme while keeping decorative counts subordinate, and recheck at 390px.

findings.evidence: The profile header ends with a bare pencil glyph at the far right, while the Body card below uses a labeled 'Edit' control with the same icon. These are the screen's only edit entry points.
findings.userConsequence: The name and summary edit action can read as decoration and be missed; a user may assume only the Body fields are editable.
findings.suggestedChange: Add a visible 'Edit' label to the header action or reuse the labeled Body pattern for both.

findings.evidence: The bodyweight card plots three marked points with date labels but no vertical scale or point values; the only numbers are in the caption (Starting 169 · Current 168 · Change −1 · Range 168–169).
findings.userConsequence: The line's slope can be over-read, and the chart adds little beyond the caption for a 1 lb change.
findings.suggestedChange: Add min/max axis labels or small value labels at the three points, keeping the point markers and honest nonzero scale.

findings.evidence: History rows end with 'last 10/26' for every recent movement, and the exercise-history sheet labels sessions 'Oct 26 (Mon)' and 'Oct 19 (Mon)' without a year.
findings.userConsequence: Once logs span more than one year, users cannot tell this October from last October when comparing sessions.
findings.suggestedChange: Include the year when it is not the current year, either in the row metadata or the session header.

findings.evidence: At the captured scroll position the sticky Back/Save program footer cuts across the Weekly preview: the third day card begins under the footer and no bottom clearance is visible. The two earlier day cards end cleanly above it.
findings.userConsequence: A user reviewing before saving may think only two days were imported or miss the third day's exercises.
findings.suggestedChange: Reserve footer-height bottom padding in the scroll area so a complete day card can clear the footer while the actions stay sticky.

strengths: Prompts puts Copy prompt with its character count and Go to Import above collapsed coach prose, so the offline copy/paste workflow is the first visible task.

The four import states are plainly differentiated: a counted JSON editor, a bordered recovery alert with Copy as primary, a gated Resolve step, and a confirmation that names the catalog link and says further review is optional.

Mobile workout now shows every exercise's set row in the first viewport with 15px set values, 13px prescriptions, labeled History and More, and a bordered rest-edit control; the saved 6/6 status and Finish workout action stay visible.
Routine overview names the next day and week, opens the week containing it, marks 'Next workout' in the list, and keeps analysis to a single summary row.
The desktop shell is stable: persistent sidebar, one content origin and measure, no duplicate hamburger; workout tools stay near exercise names and routine actions group with their row.
History rows now have real separators and trailing chevrons, explicit sort labels, and legible metadata; export filters stack to one column, counts are summarized, and Copy/Download remain clear.
Workspace surfaces Theme before the long storage explanation, keeps Download backup dominant, styles destructive import distinctly, and states local-first limits in plain language.
Light and dark captures share structure and semantics; navigation pairs consistent line icons with labels, and the session summary and onboarding each give one obvious next action.
limitations: Static 390x844 and 1280x900 captures only; keyboard, focus, screen-reader, tap-target, persistence and scrolling behavior were not tested.
Dark evidence covers four screens and desktop evidence four routes; other states at those themes and widths are unverified.
Contrast is a visual judgment only; no ratios were measured. The terminal-theme finding is a comparative visual impression.
Workspace's Request protection button and the remaining Appearance controls are below the fold in both themes, so their stated fixes cannot be confirmed here.
Warm-up 'Set rest' without a prescribed duration and the paired 'rest 90s' / '1:30' displays were treated as intentional data-driven states, not defects.
Baseline captures were reopened only for mobile workout, dark workout and mobile History comparisons; this was not a full image-to-image audit.
All 27 manifest files were present, hash-verified against the manifest, and opened directly as images.
Prior-round reviews, all four assessments and the round-4 implementation response were read; no other current-round output, source edits, app interaction or delegation occurred.
